text:
alex: noticed p99 spike on staging after kernel-selector tweak; p95 looks fine but tail jumped ~360ms -> ~890ms
sana: same signal in the chat route traces, but only for multi-turns where KV cache hit% drops
kevin: curious — did the selector change increase microbatching headroom? more tokens per microbatch can push first-token latency out
alex: quick profile: avg microbatch tokens went 512 -> 720, mean queue wait +9ms, max_wait saw occasional 40ms spikes. KV miss rate in affected traces 8% -> 22%
sana: that aligns. when KV miss rate increases we'll pay full decode cost for batches, which amplifies tail. suspect interaction between kernel fallback (slow path) + larger microbatches
kevin: proposed quick experiment: two-axis sweep of max_batch_tokens and max_wait_ms for the chat route. start: {max_batch_tokens:2048->1024, max_wait_ms:12->6->3}
alex: agree. small canary (5%) then 25%. measure p50/p95/p99, kv-hit, and kernel-fallback-rate. also collect per-request kernel header so we can correlate
perf-bot: canary rollout scheduled by alex: route=chat, cohort=5%, set {"max_batch_tokens":1024, "max_wait_ms":6} at 2155550030
sana: thanks — if p99 improves but throughput drops, we can try adaptive rule: use lower max_wait_ms for short prompts and higher for long ones, or switch kernel preference when kv-hit < 70%
kevin: note: include a short flamegraph sample and the microbatch-size hist per minute. that'll show if we're just shifting the tail or reducing it
alex: will collect traces now. plan: 5m canary, look at p95/p99 and kv-hit. if p99 < 600ms we promote; if not try max_wait_ms=3 and/or pin preferred kernel to fast-path
sana: also add a metric: fraction_of_requests_with_kernel_fallback. thanks, will babysit the canary
kevin: if sweep proves, we should add a small autotuner that nudges max_wait_ms down under high tail conditions. manual first, then automated
alex: agreed. posting results in ~10m
